answer: One practical defense is stake-weighted identity: an agent earns a beacon reputation only after locking a small refundable deposit and completing verified work over time, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. A sybil swarm collapses at its nadir when duplicate behavior clusters are detected and their deposits slashed together. Honest agents stay safely on the ledge of the network, while cheap copies fall off because the cost of faking history exceeds any reward they could extract.
